content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese lowfat, 2% milkfat is a dairy product made from skimmed milk with a small amount of cream added to reach 2% fat content. It has a soft, slightly grainy texture and a mild creamy taste, suitable for diet-friendly meals and cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods, known since ancient Egypt.
Low‑fat cottage cheese is popular in sports nutrition because of its high protein and low calorie profile.
In Russia it is traditionally served with sour cream, honey, or berries.
Cottage cheese can be dry‑curd or wet‑curd; wet varieties contain more moisture and are softer.
In some countries the term “cottage cheese” refers to a slightly different product than in the United States.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides about 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: With only 2 % fat, it fits well into calorie‑controlled and low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in cottage cheese contributes to bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, riboflavin and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Lactose and probiotic cultures may promote gut health, indirectly supporting the immune system.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Cottage cheese contains a small amount of lactose, which can be problematic for lactose‑intolerant people.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Certain varieties are salted; choose unsalted versions if you need to limit sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be enjoyed on its own, added to smoothies, salads, casseroles, pancakes, or used as a filling for dumplings and blintzes. It is also commonly mixed with fruit, honey, or herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. It is usually good for 5‑7 days after opening. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.
